t: This is the Bank of England building, a landmark of the City of London. Two architects matter here. Sir John Soane, a bricklayer's son who rose to the top of his profession, designed it. He specialised in the Neo-Classical style, became professor of architecture at the Royal Academy, and was knighted in 1831. Later, Sir Herbert Baker also designed it. Baker was among the most prominent and prolific architects of his generation, and is remembered above all for his work in South Africa, where he developed a Neo-Classical style meant to project strength and permanence.
